opportunity: A LOAD narrower than its pointer's pointee printed as a read of the whole field or element, truncated or masked: `(unsigned short)a0->field_0x8` for `movzwl 8(%rdi)`, `(a0->field_0x48 & 0x2000) != 0` for `testb $0x20,0x49(%rbx)`, `(int)a0[a1]` for a 4-byte read of a `long` element. The value is the same on little-endian, but the printed C reads bytes the program never reads and faults when the object ends at the last byte the program reads (a page end).

root_cause: RuleExpandLoad (cleanup pool) rewrites a LOAD narrower than its pointer's pointee as a LOAD of the whole pointee and takes the bytes back out with a SUBPIECE (truncation form) or inside `(V & C) == D` compares (AND form). elemptr (#731) kept the load narrow only when no type-locked Varnode sat at the base of the pointer chain, and only with elemptr on; every remaining site on main is behind a lock (a structsynth parameter, a declared prototype), and with elemptr off every inferred pointer and every declared record reached through a call result or a loop phi widened too.
fix: The truncation form is never taken. The AND form is taken only when the widened pointer is a PTRSUB field of a record or union a declaration laid out (not a structsynth-minted record, not a bare pointer's target or an array element) AND that pointer reaches a type-locked Varnode through PTRADD/PTRSUB/INT_ADD/COPY/CAST alone (elemptr's former keeps_load_narrow walk, now without the elemptr gate): p3_dataflow/kuna_narrowload.rs widens_into_declared_field. A declared record reached through a call's result, a loop's phi or a loaded pointer keeps its narrow read. kuna_elemptr::keeps_load_narrow is removed. Nothing widens a STORE (TypeOpStore::getInputCast casts the pointer of a narrow store); the fixture's 1-, 2- and 4-byte stores at a page end are checked.
roundtrip: narrowload_x86_64.c: 17 functions read/write 1, 2 and 4 bytes of wider record fields and elements; main passes objects that end at the last byte touched, at a page end. decompile-project with elemptr on and off, printed functions compiled with gcc and clang against the export header and linked with the fixture's own prelude/main: main's kuna -> SIGSEGV on all 16 (4 builds x 2 compilers x 2 arms); fix -> all 16 print what the binary prints. narrowload_dwarf_x86_64.c (-g): 3 functions mask one byte of a declared record's 4-byte field through a call's result, a loop's phi and a loaded pointer, each object ending at that byte at a page end; runs print `1 0 2 1`. main 632437155: elemptr on 8/8 OK, elemptr off 8/8 SIGSEGV; the previous head (AND form gated on the declared record alone) 16/16 SIGSEGV; this fix 16/16 OK. With the lock walk disabled the test fails: `gcc_O0 on: a narrow read printed wide, as 0x8100`.

corpus_diff.classification: every changed function holds a RuleExpandLoad site of the main build; every changed line is that site re-spelled at its own width, or (tar O2-noinline 0x37190, e2fsck O2 0x2bb10, bash O2 0x8bad0, and 29 elemptr-off functions) the narrow read becoming its own statement or printed at its uses instead of through a truncated temporary, which renumbers variables and, with elemptr off, gives a variable the read's width (sort O2 0x7af0 `long v2 = a0[10]` -> `int v2 = *(int *)&a0[10]`). No signature, argument count or exported variable count changes on any corpus; variables[] is identical on the 45 default binaries.
corpus_diff.residual_width_check: a per-instruction check (final LOAD/STORE wider than every access of the instruction's own p-code) finds only merges of adjacent reads that read the same bytes (gzip SH() byte pairs, 16-byte pairs of 8-byte reads): 0 stores, 0 widened loads of the class

corpus_diff.declared_record_residual: The AND form still widens a declared record's field reached from a type-locked parameter or global: 0 sites on every stripped corpus (castbench 45, disjoint 28), 182 loads in 81 functions on the 18 DWARF builds, exactly the loads main widened (e.g. a DWARF-typed `r` in `(r->flags & 0x81) == 0x80`). The printed C reads the whole declared field there, which faults only for an object shorter than its declared type.
